---
name: gap-count-vs-gap-cost
description: An item recorded as "untouched, separate gap" across many files may share its residue with a gap already reduced — check whose hypothesis it needs, not whether anyone mentioned it
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When several files agree that item X is "untouched / single-field only / a separate gap", that
consensus records who *wrote about* X, not what X *costs*. Cluster P's global generation was
labelled single-field in five AJC files, each giving the correct reason (generation comes off the
dévissage slice, not the peel, so it is no corollary of vanishing). None of them asked the next
question: *whose hypothesis does the slice need at the base-changed object?* It was the same base
vanishing the already-reduced item's one open input supplies. So generation was never a second
gap — one input bought all three cluster-P statements at the same threshold.

**Why:** a correct reason for "not a corollary" gets copied forward as if it were a reason for
"not reachable". The two are different claims, and the second is never re-measured because the
first is true.

**How to apply:** for each gap listed as separate, read the *hypothesis* of the theorem that would
close it and compare it to the hypotheses already discharged elsewhere. If they match, the gap
count is wrong even though every individual file was honest. Related:
[[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]], [[prescriptions-need-auditing-like-measurements]],
[[absence-claims-need-the-whole-project]].
